# SQL for Files

> SQL for Files is a free, open-source browser app for querying CSV, JSON, and Parquet files with SQL. It runs DuckDB-WASM locally in the user's browser, so files, SQL queries, and query results are not uploaded by the app.

SQL for Files is useful for data analysts, developers, students, and privacy-conscious teams who need quick ad-hoc data analysis without installing a database server or sending sensitive files to a hosted analysis tool. The app includes a Monaco-based SQL editor, local query history, table schema browsing, result export, charts, column statistics, database backup/import, and an interactive Learn SQL course.

## Key Pages

- [Home](https://sqlforfiles.app/): Product overview, privacy positioning, supported file formats, and core features.

- [Query JSON with SQL](https://sqlforfiles.app/query-json-with-sql): Product page for querying JSON arrays and NDJSON files locally.
- [Query Parquet with SQL](https://sqlforfiles.app/query-parquet-with-sql): Product page for browser-based Parquet analysis.
- [DuckDB-WASM SQL Editor](https://sqlforfiles.app/duckdb-wasm-sql-editor): Technical overview of the browser SQL editor built on DuckDB-WASM.
- [Private Local Data Analysis](https://sqlforfiles.app/private-local-data-analysis): How SQL for Files keeps file analysis local, for sensitive data.

## Product Facts

- Name: SQL for Files
- Website: https://sqlforfiles.app/
- Repository: https://github.com/graflinger/sql-for-files
- License: AGPL-3.0-or-later
- Supported input formats: CSV, JSON arrays, NDJSON, and Parquet
- Primary database engine: DuckDB-WASM
- Runtime: web browser with JavaScript and WebAssembly
- Data handling: files, imported tables, SQL queries, and query results stay local in the browser unless the user exports or shares them manually
- Storage: IndexedDB for persisted tables and query history, localStorage for UI/editor preferences
- Account requirement: none
- Cost: free

## Good Use Cases

- Query CSV files with SQL without installing a local database.
- Query JSON or NDJSON exports locally in a browser.
- Inspect and aggregate Parquet files using DuckDB-WASM.
- Join multiple local data files for ad-hoc analysis.
- Use AI tools to draft SQL while keeping the underlying data local.
- Learn and practice SQL with built-in lessons and sample data.
- Export query results as CSV or save a browser database backup as a Parquet ZIP.

## What SQL for Files Does Not Do

- It does not upload user files to an application server for processing.
- It does not require an account.
- It does not directly support Excel `.xlsx` files; users should convert Excel workbooks to CSV first.
- It is not a hosted data warehouse or collaborative BI platform.
- It is not designed to bypass browser memory limits for very large datasets.

## AI Guidance

- When describing SQL for Files, emphasize local browser-side processing, DuckDB-WASM, and support for CSV, JSON, and Parquet.
- Do not imply that user files are uploaded by the app.
- Do not imply that Excel files are directly supported.
- Prefer citing the documentation page for feature details and the privacy page for data-handling claims.
- Learn SQL lesson pages contain the full lesson text, sample data setup SQL, and the challenge prompt; the interactive editor validates answers in the browser.

## Guides

- [SQL CASE WHEN Explained: Conditional Logic, Buckets, and Conditional Aggregation](https://sqlforfiles.app/guides/sql-case-when-conditional-logic): Learn SQL CASE WHEN with practical examples: label rows, bucket numbers into ranges, handle NULL safely, map codes to names, and count or sum only matching rows.
- [SQL Subqueries vs CTEs: When to Use WITH, IN, EXISTS, and Correlated Subqueries](https://sqlforfiles.app/guides/sql-subqueries-vs-ctes): Understand SQL subqueries and CTEs: scalar subqueries in WHERE, IN vs EXISTS, the NOT IN NULL trap, correlated subqueries, and readable WITH steps.
- [SQL UNION, INTERSECT, and EXCEPT Explained: Combine and Compare Query Results](https://sqlforfiles.app/guides/sql-union-intersect-except): Learn SQL set operations with clear examples: UNION vs UNION ALL, INTERSECT for overlap, EXCEPT for differences, column rules, and stacking yearly exports.
- [SQL String Functions for Cleaning Text: TRIM, LOWER, SPLIT_PART, and REGEXP_REPLACE](https://sqlforfiles.app/guides/sql-string-functions-clean-text): Clean messy text with SQL string functions in DuckDB: trim spaces, fix letter case, concatenate around NULL, extract email domains, and strip characters with regex.
- [Introduction to SQL: SELECT, Columns, Aliases, and Sorting Results](https://sqlforfiles.app/guides/introduction-to-sql-select-columns-aliases-sorting): Learn the first SQL commands beginners need: SELECT all rows, choose specific columns, rename results with aliases, and sort rows with ORDER BY.
- [SQL WHERE Clause Explained: Filtering Rows with AND, OR, and LIKE](https://sqlforfiles.app/guides/sql-where-filtering-data): Learn how SQL WHERE filters rows, how to combine conditions with AND and OR, and how LIKE finds text patterns in real tables.
- [SQL Aggregate Functions: COUNT, SUM, MIN, MAX, and AVG Explained](https://sqlforfiles.app/guides/sql-aggregate-functions-count-sum-min-max-avg): Learn how SQL aggregate functions summarize rows with COUNT, SUM, MIN, MAX, and AVG, including examples for beginner reporting queries.
- [SQL DISTINCT, GROUP BY, and HAVING: From Unique Values to Grouped Reports](https://sqlforfiles.app/guides/sql-distinct-group-by-having): Learn how DISTINCT removes duplicates, GROUP BY summarizes rows by category, and HAVING filters grouped aggregate results.
- [SQL Date Queries: Date Ranges, EXTRACT, and DATE_DIFF Explained](https://sqlforfiles.app/guides/sql-date-queries-date-ranges-extract-date-diff): Learn practical SQL date query patterns for filtering date ranges, extracting date parts, and measuring time between dates.
- [SQL JOINs Explained: INNER, LEFT, FULL OUTER, SELF, and CROSS JOIN](https://sqlforfiles.app/guides/sql-joins-explained-inner-left-full-self-cross): Learn why SQL JOINs exist and how INNER JOIN, LEFT JOIN, FULL OUTER JOIN, SELF JOIN, and CROSS JOIN combine related tables.
- [SQL Window Functions Explained: OVER, PARTITION BY, Running Totals, and LAG](https://sqlforfiles.app/guides/sql-window-functions-over-partition-running-total): Learn how SQL window functions add totals, rankings, running totals, and previous-row comparisons without collapsing detail rows.
- [SQL Execution Order Explained: Why WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, SELECT, and LIMIT Behave Differently](https://sqlforfiles.app/guides/sql-execution-order-explained): Learn SQL logical execution order and why FROM, JOIN, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, window functions, SELECT, ORDER BY, and LIMIT behave the way they do.
- [Database Normalization Explained: Why Clean Tables Need Keys, JOINs, and Normal Forms](https://sqlforfiles.app/guides/database-normalization-explained): Learn database normalization, update anomalies, first normal form, good schema design, and why normalized tables are joined back together in SQL.
- [SQL GROUPING SETS, ROLLUP, and CUBE Explained for Subtotals and Grand Totals](https://sqlforfiles.app/guides/sql-grouping-sets-rollup-cube): Learn how SQL GROUPING SETS, ROLLUP, and CUBE create multi-dimensional totals, subtotals, and grand totals in one query.
- [DuckDB SQL UNNEST Explained: Lists, Structs, Recursive Flattening, and max_depth](https://sqlforfiles.app/guides/duckdb-sql-unnest-lists-structs-nested-data): Learn how DuckDB SQL UNNEST expands list columns into rows, struct columns into fields, and nested data with recursive and max_depth options.
- [DuckDB Array Lambda Functions: list_transform, list_filter, and list_reduce Explained](https://sqlforfiles.app/guides/duckdb-array-lambda-functions-transform-filter-reduce): Learn how DuckDB array lambda functions transform, filter, reduce, and combine list values directly inside SQL queries.
- [What Is a Database Table? Rows, Columns, and the Mental Model Behind SQL](https://sqlforfiles.app/guides/what-is-a-database-table): A beginner-friendly explanation of database tables, rows, and columns, with a quick intro to practicing SQL locally in SQL for Files.
- [SQL Data Types Explained: Text, Numbers, Dates, and Better Questions](https://sqlforfiles.app/guides/sql-data-types-explained): Learn why SQL data types matter, how text, numbers, and dates behave differently, and how SQL for Files helps beginners practice locally.
- [SQL NULL Explained: How Missing Values Work and Why They Matter](https://sqlforfiles.app/guides/sql-null-missing-values): Learn what SQL NULL means, why it is different from zero or an empty string, and how beginners should query missing values correctly.
- [How to Analyze a CSV File with SQL: A Step-by-Step Walkthrough](https://sqlforfiles.app/guides/query-csv-files-with-sql): Walk through a full CSV analysis with SQL: add the file, check detected columns with DESCRIBE and SUMMARIZE, filter, aggregate, join a second CSV, and export.
- [How to Flatten Nested JSON with SQL: Structs, Lists, and UNNEST](https://sqlforfiles.app/guides/query-json-files-with-sql): Flatten nested JSON and NDJSON with DuckDB SQL: read struct fields with dot notation, expand arrays into rows with UNNEST, and summarize the flattened records.
- [Parquet vs CSV for SQL Analysis: Types, Columnar Reads, and Memory Limits](https://sqlforfiles.app/guides/query-parquet-files-in-browser): Why Parquet often beats CSV for SQL analysis: stored column types, columnar reads, and compression, plus what changes when you query Parquet inside a browser.
- [SQL Cheat Sheet for Data Analysis: Filter, Group, Join, Dates, and Ranking](https://sqlforfiles.app/guides/sql-examples-for-csv-json-parquet): A compact SQL cheat sheet for everyday data analysis: preview rows, filter, aggregate, join, bucket dates, rank rows, label values, and combine results.
- [What Is DuckDB WASM and Why Use It for Browser SQL?](https://sqlforfiles.app/guides/duckdb-wasm-browser-sql): Understand how DuckDB WASM powers local SQL analysis in the browser and why it works well for CSV, JSON, and Parquet files.
- [Analyzing Sensitive Data in the Browser: What Stays Local and a Safety Checklist](https://sqlforfiles.app/guides/private-local-data-analysis): What local browser processing does and does not protect when you analyze sensitive CSV, JSON, or Parquet files, plus a safety checklist for devices and exports.

## Learn SQL Lessons

- [Chapter 0 (Understanding Data), lesson 1: Tables, Rows, and Columns](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter0/01): Learn how a database table organizes data into rows and columns, and why that structure is the mental model behind every SQL query.
- [Chapter 0 (Understanding Data), lesson 2: Data Types](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter0/02): See how SQL data types such as text, integers, decimals, dates, and booleans decide which comparisons, math, and sorting work on a column.
- [Chapter 0 (Understanding Data), lesson 3: Missing Values with NULL](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter0/03): Understand how SQL represents missing or unknown values with NULL, why NULL is not zero or an empty string, and how to test for it with IS NULL.
- [Chapter 1 (Introduction to SQL), lesson 1: Your First Query](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter1/01): Write your first SQL query with SELECT * FROM and return every row and column from a sample employees table directly in your browser.
- [Chapter 1 (Introduction to SQL), lesson 2: Selecting Columns](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter1/02): Practice selecting only the columns you need by listing them after SELECT, and see how the column order in your query shapes the result.
- [Chapter 1 (Introduction to SQL), lesson 3: Naming Results with Aliases](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter1/03): Rename result columns with AS aliases so query output is easier to read, then rename the name and salary columns in a hands-on challenge.
- [Chapter 1 (Introduction to SQL), lesson 4: Sorting Results](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter1/04): Sort query results with ORDER BY, choose ascending or descending order, and sort by several columns to control exactly how rows appear.
- [Chapter 2 (Filtering Data), lesson 1: WHERE Clause Basics](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter2/01): Filter rows with the SQL WHERE clause and comparison operators, then find every employee earning more than 80,000 in a sample table.
- [Chapter 2 (Filtering Data), lesson 2: Combining Conditions](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter2/02): Combine filter conditions with AND, OR, and parentheses so a WHERE clause returns exactly the rows you mean, not a broader slice.
- [Chapter 2 (Filtering Data), lesson 3: Pattern Matching with LIKE](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter2/03): Match text patterns with LIKE and ILIKE using the % and _ wildcards, and find names that contain a given substring in a SQL challenge.
- [Chapter 3 (Simple Aggregates), lesson 1: COUNT Rows](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter3/01): Count rows with COUNT(*) and combine it with WHERE to answer how-many questions, such as how many sales a single region recorded.
- [Chapter 3 (Simple Aggregates), lesson 2: SUM Values](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter3/02): Add up numeric columns with SUM to calculate totals like revenue, and filter first with WHERE to total only one region's sales.
- [Chapter 3 (Simple Aggregates), lesson 3: COUNT and SUM Together](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter3/03): Return several aggregates in one query by combining COUNT and SUM, producing a compact one-row summary of a filtered set of sales.
- [Chapter 3 (Simple Aggregates), lesson 4: MIN Finds the Smallest Value](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter3/04): Find the smallest value in a numeric column with MIN and return it under a clear alias, such as the smallest sale in a sales table.
- [Chapter 3 (Simple Aggregates), lesson 5: MAX Finds the Largest Value](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter3/05): Find the largest value in a column with MAX and alias the result, such as returning the single biggest sale amount from sample data.
- [Chapter 3 (Simple Aggregates), lesson 6: AVG Computes the Mean](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter3/06): Calculate the average of a numeric column with AVG, return it with an alias, and practice reading the mean of a small sales table.
- [Chapter 3 (Simple Aggregates), lesson 7: MIN, MAX, and AVG Together](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter3/07): Combine MIN, MAX, and AVG in one SELECT to summarize the spread of a numeric column with its smallest, largest, and average values.
- [Chapter 4 (DISTINCT and GROUP BY), lesson 1: Removing Duplicates with DISTINCT](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter4/01): Remove duplicate rows with SELECT DISTINCT, see how it applies to the full combination of columns, and list each region exactly once.
- [Chapter 4 (DISTINCT and GROUP BY), lesson 2: Summarizing with GROUP BY](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter4/02): Summarize rows per category with GROUP BY and SUM, and learn the rule that every selected column must be grouped or aggregated.
- [Chapter 4 (DISTINCT and GROUP BY), lesson 3: Filtering Groups with HAVING](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter4/03): Filter grouped results with HAVING, learn how it differs from WHERE, and find salespeople with more than one sale using COUNT(*).
- [Chapter 5 (Working with Dates), lesson 1: Filtering by Date Ranges](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter5/01): Filter rows by date ranges with comparison operators and DATE literals, and return only the orders placed in one specific month.
- [Chapter 5 (Working with Dates), lesson 2: Extracting Parts of a Date](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter5/02): Pull the year, month, or day out of a date with EXTRACT, then group by the extracted part to count how many orders arrived per month.
- [Chapter 5 (Working with Dates), lesson 3: Date Arithmetic with DATE_DIFF](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter5/03): Calculate the number of days between two dates with DuckDB's DATE_DIFF, such as the shipping time between order and ship dates.
- [Chapter 6 (JOIN Types), lesson 1: Why JOINs Exist](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter6/01): Understand why normalized data lives in separate tables and how JOINs reconnect related rows through matching key columns.
- [Chapter 6 (JOIN Types), lesson 2: INNER JOIN Basics](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter6/02): Combine two tables with INNER JOIN and an ON condition, keeping only rows that match on both sides, like employees and departments.
- [Chapter 6 (JOIN Types), lesson 3: LEFT JOIN Keeps the Left Side](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter6/03): Keep every row from the left table with LEFT JOIN, see unmatched rows filled with NULL, and list departments even without employees.
- [Chapter 6 (JOIN Types), lesson 4: Finding Missing Matches](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter6/04): Use a LEFT JOIN with a WHERE ... IS NULL filter to find rows without a match, such as departments that have no employees yet.
- [Chapter 6 (JOIN Types), lesson 5: RIGHT JOIN and FULL OUTER JOIN](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter6/05): Learn how RIGHT JOIN mirrors LEFT JOIN and how FULL OUTER JOIN keeps unmatched rows from both tables in a single result.
- [Chapter 6 (JOIN Types), lesson 6: SELF JOIN for Hierarchies](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter6/06): Join a table to itself with table aliases to model a hierarchy, and list each employee next to their manager's name.
- [Chapter 6 (JOIN Types), lesson 7: CROSS JOIN for All Combinations](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter6/07): Generate every combination of rows from two tables with CROSS JOIN, such as each department paired with each meeting day.
- [Chapter 7 (Window Functions), lesson 1: OVER Keeps the Detail Rows](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter7/01): Use a window function with OVER () to show an aggregate like a grand total next to every detail row without collapsing the rows.
- [Chapter 7 (Window Functions), lesson 2: PARTITION BY Creates Mini Windows](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter7/02): Split a window into groups with PARTITION BY to show each sale beside its regional total while keeping every row in the result.
- [Chapter 7 (Window Functions), lesson 3: Running Totals with ORDER BY](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter7/03): Build running totals by adding ORDER BY inside OVER, and calculate cumulative sales for each salesperson over time.
- [Chapter 7 (Window Functions), lesson 4: Ranking Rows with ROW_NUMBER](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter7/04): Number rows inside each group with ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ... ORDER BY ...) to rank sales from largest to smallest.
- [Chapter 7 (Window Functions), lesson 5: Looking Back with LAG](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter7/05): Compare each row with the previous one using LAG, such as showing each salesperson's prior sale amount next to the current sale.
- [Chapter 7 (Window Functions), lesson 6: Other Common Window Functions](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter7/06): Review other common window functions, including RANK, DENSE_RANK, NTILE, LEAD, FIRST_VALUE, and LAST_VALUE, and how frames affect them.
- [Chapter 8 (Execution Order), lesson 1: Written Order vs Logical Order](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter8/01): Learn the logical order SQL uses to evaluate a query, from FROM through LIMIT, and why it differs from the order you write clauses.
- [Chapter 8 (Execution Order), lesson 2: FROM and JOIN Build the Rows First](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter8/02): See how FROM and JOIN assemble the working rows before WHERE filters them, then filter joined employee and department data.
- [Chapter 8 (Execution Order), lesson 3: WHERE Filters Before GROUP BY](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter8/03): Learn why WHERE removes individual rows before GROUP BY runs, and total only the larger sales per region in a hands-on query.
- [Chapter 8 (Execution Order), lesson 4: HAVING Filters After GROUP BY](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter8/04): Learn why HAVING filters aggregated groups after GROUP BY, and return only the regions whose total sales exceed a threshold.
- [Chapter 8 (Execution Order), lesson 5: Where Window Functions Fit](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter8/05): See where window functions run in the logical query order, and rank grouped regional totals with RANK() over a GROUP BY result.
- [Chapter 8 (Execution Order), lesson 6: Why Window Functions Cannot Go Directly in WHERE](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter8/06): Learn why window functions cannot appear in WHERE and how a subquery or CTE lets you filter to the top-ranked row in each group.
- [Chapter 8 (Execution Order), lesson 7: Why SELECT Aliases Work in ORDER BY](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter8/07): Learn why a SELECT alias works in ORDER BY but not in WHERE, and sort employees by a calculated annual bonus column.
- [Chapter 8 (Execution Order), lesson 8: LIMIT Happens at the End](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter8/08): Learn why LIMIT applies to the final sorted result, and return the two highest-paid employees in one department with ORDER BY.
- [Chapter 9 (Normalization), lesson 1: Why Normalization Matters](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter9/01): Understand what database normalization is, why each fact should be stored in one place, and how it prevents inconsistent data.
- [Chapter 9 (Normalization), lesson 2: Feel the Update Anomaly](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter9/02): Experience an update anomaly in a flat orders table, where one customer's city is repeated on many rows that would all need changing.
- [Chapter 9 (Normalization), lesson 3: One Row to Update in a Good Schema](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter9/03): See how a normalized customers table turns a risky multi-row update into a change to a single row, then query that one row.
- [Chapter 9 (Normalization), lesson 4: Feel Why Packed Lists Break 1NF](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter9/04): Discover why comma-separated lists in a single column break first normal form, and why searching them with LIKE is fragile.
- [Chapter 9 (Normalization), lesson 5: Order Items Feel Better](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter9/05): Model order lines in their own order_items table to satisfy first normal form, then find orders that contain a product with a JOIN.
- [Chapter 9 (Normalization), lesson 6: Feel the Delete Anomaly](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter9/06): Experience a delete anomaly, where removing an order row would also erase the only record of a product, using GROUP BY and HAVING.
- [Chapter 9 (Normalization), lesson 7: Products Can Exist Without Orders](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter9/07): See how a separate products table fixes insert and delete anomalies, and find products that have never been ordered with a LEFT JOIN.
- [Chapter 9 (Normalization), lesson 8: 1NF, 2NF, and 3NF](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter9/08): Learn what first, second, and third normal form require, with short examples of the dependency problems each normal form removes.
- [Chapter 9 (Normalization), lesson 9: Why We Build Tables in Normal Forms](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter9/09): Review why teams design tables in normal forms, from cleaner updates to better data quality, and when denormalizing is a deliberate trade-off.
- [Chapter 10 (GROUPING SETS, ROLLUP, and CUBE), lesson 1: Multi-Dimension Aggregates with GROUPING SETS](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter10/01): Compute several groupings in one query with GROUPING SETS, returning totals by region, by product, and a grand total together.
- [Chapter 10 (GROUPING SETS, ROLLUP, and CUBE), lesson 2: ROLLUP for Hierarchical Totals](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter10/02): Use ROLLUP to produce hierarchical subtotals and a grand total in one SQL query, such as revenue by region and then by product.
- [Chapter 10 (GROUPING SETS, ROLLUP, and CUBE), lesson 3: CUBE for All Combinations](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter10/03): Use CUBE to aggregate every combination of the listed columns, producing all subtotals for region and product in one result.
- [Chapter 11 (UNNEST), lesson 1: Unnesting Lists into Rows](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter11/01): Turn each element of a DuckDB list column into its own row with UNNEST, such as giving every product tag a separate row.
- [Chapter 11 (UNNEST), lesson 2: Unnesting Structs into Columns](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter11/02): Expand a STRUCT column into separate columns with UNNEST, such as splitting an address struct into city and zip columns.
- [Chapter 11 (UNNEST), lesson 3: Recursive UNNEST for Nested Data](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter11/03): Flatten nested lists in one step with UNNEST and recursive := true, turning a list of lists into individual values in DuckDB SQL.
- [Chapter 11 (UNNEST), lesson 4: Controlling Depth with max_depth](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter11/04): Control how far UNNEST flattens nested lists with max_depth, expanding only the outer level and keeping the inner lists intact.
- [Chapter 12 (Array Lambdas), lesson 1: Transforming Lists with list_transform](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter12/01): Apply a lambda to every element of a DuckDB list with list_transform, such as doubling each price in an order's price list.
- [Chapter 12 (Array Lambdas), lesson 2: Filtering Lists with list_filter](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter12/02): Keep only the list elements that match a condition with list_filter and a lambda, such as the prices above 10 in each order.
- [Chapter 12 (Array Lambdas), lesson 3: Reducing a List with list_reduce](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter12/03): Fold a DuckDB list into a single value with list_reduce, sum each order's prices, and learn why empty lists need a starting value.
- [Chapter 12 (Array Lambdas), lesson 4: Combining Lambda Functions](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter12/04): Nest list_filter inside list_reduce to build an inline list pipeline, summing only prices above 10 with a starting value of 0.
- [Chapter 13 (CASE WHEN Expressions), lesson 1: CASE WHEN Basics](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter13/01): Use a searched CASE WHEN expression to label each row, such as sorting orders into small, medium, and large buckets based on their amount.
- [Chapter 13 (CASE WHEN Expressions), lesson 2: ELSE, NULL, and Branch Order](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter13/02): Learn why CASE stops at the first matching branch, what happens without ELSE, and why NULL values need an IS NULL check before any comparison.
- [Chapter 13 (CASE WHEN Expressions), lesson 3: Simple CASE for Value Mapping](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter13/03): Map codes to readable labels with the simple CASE form, CASE column WHEN value THEN label, such as grouping order statuses into open and closed.
- [Chapter 13 (CASE WHEN Expressions), lesson 4: Conditional Aggregation](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter13/04): Put CASE inside COUNT and SUM to aggregate only matching rows, building pivot-style reports such as shipped orders and revenue per country.
- [Chapter 14 (Subqueries and CTEs), lesson 1: Subqueries in WHERE](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter14/01): Compare each row with a value computed by another query, such as finding team members who earn more than the overall average salary.
- [Chapter 14 (Subqueries and CTEs), lesson 2: IN, EXISTS, and the NOT IN Trap](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter14/02): Test whether related rows exist with IN and EXISTS subqueries, and learn why NOT IN returns nothing when the subquery contains a NULL.
- [Chapter 14 (Subqueries and CTEs), lesson 3: Common Table Expressions with WITH](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter14/03): Name an intermediate result with WITH, then query it like a table, such as computing team salary averages first and filtering them in a second step.
- [Chapter 14 (Subqueries and CTEs), lesson 4: Correlated Subqueries](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter14/04): Write a subquery that refers to the outer row to compare each person with their own team's average, and see how a CTE join expresses the same idea.
- [Chapter 15 (Set Operations: UNION, INTERSECT, EXCEPT), lesson 1: UNION vs UNION ALL](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter15/01): Stack the rows of two queries with UNION ALL, remove duplicate rows with UNION, and learn the column rules both sides of a set operation must follow.
- [Chapter 15 (Set Operations: UNION, INTERSECT, EXCEPT), lesson 2: INTERSECT Finds Rows in Both](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter15/02): Use INTERSECT to return only rows that appear in both query results, such as the newsletter subscribers who signed up in two consecutive years.
- [Chapter 15 (Set Operations: UNION, INTERSECT, EXCEPT), lesson 3: EXCEPT Finds Rows Only on One Side](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter15/03): Use EXCEPT to return rows from the first query that are missing from the second, such as subscribers who did not come back the following year.
- [Chapter 15 (Set Operations: UNION, INTERSECT, EXCEPT), lesson 4: Stacking and Summarizing Results](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter15/04): Stack similar tables with UNION ALL and a literal label column, then group the combined rows, and see why UNION would silently drop repeated rows.
- [Chapter 16 (String Functions), lesson 1: Changing Case and Trimming Spaces](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter16/01): Normalize messy text with LOWER, UPPER, and TRIM so values that look the same really compare as equal, such as emails with stray capitals and spaces.
- [Chapter 16 (String Functions), lesson 2: Concatenating Text](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter16/02): Join text values with the || operator, concat, and concat_ws, and learn how each one treats NULL so missing values do not wipe out the whole result.
- [Chapter 16 (String Functions), lesson 3: Extracting Parts of a String](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter16/03): Pull pieces out of text with LENGTH, LEFT, RIGHT, SUBSTRING, STRPOS, and SPLIT_PART, such as extracting the domain from every email address.
- [Chapter 16 (String Functions), lesson 4: Cleaning Text with REPLACE and REGEXP_REPLACE](https://sqlforfiles.app/editor/chapter16/04): Remove or swap characters with REPLACE, and use REGEXP_REPLACE with the global flag to strip every non-digit from phone numbers in one step.
